identity.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR Corvette C6.R maps to Chevrolet's first-generation factory GT1 C6.R, which made its competition debut at Sebring in March 2005. The car used a six-speed sequential racing gearbox operated through a cockpit-mounted sequential lever in the period GT configuration; period descriptions say the driver could make flat, clutchless upshifts using an electronic ignition cut. Keep the later 2009-2013 GT2/GTE C6.R and non-factory Corvette C6-based race cars distinct. The PMR observation is pinned to Steam content build 24725083; its observed values remain simulator comparison evidence rather than real-car proof.

The official PMR GT class page names Chevrolet Corvette C6.R and frames the content as the 2004-05 GT season. General Motors' Corvette Racing history identifies the C6.R's 2005 competition debut and GT1 career. Independent C6.R technical and period racing references identify the six-speed sequential gearbox, lever operation, clutchless flat upshifts, and ignition cut. No matching curated C6.R record exists in data/v1, so this case proposes a new canonical record.

claims.basis: The official PMR GT class page names Chevrolet Corvette C6.R and frames the content as the 2004-05 GT season. Independent C6.R technical and period racing references identify the six-speed sequential gearbox, lever operation, clutchless flat upshifts, and ignition cut. Independent C6.R technical references identify a six-speed gearbox, and the PMR observation independently reports six forward gears. Both C6.R technical references explicitly identify the Xtrac transmission as sequential. The period GT selector restriction excludes paddle operation for the target era, and the C6.R operation description says shifts were made by pulling back on a lever. The reviewed technical references explicitly describe the C6.R gearbox as sequential; no H-pattern gate is documented for the target GT1 specification. The C6.R technical description explicitly attributes the shift event to an electronic ignition interrupter, which is an automatic upshift cut. The C6.R GT1 technical reference explicitly says the driver did not need the clutch pedal on upshifts. The C6.R operation description explicitly says the driver did not need to lift off the throttle for upshifts, consistent with the electronic ignition cut. driver_summary: 6-speed lever sequential. Launch clutch use is not established, so use it to be safe. Stay flat on the upshift because the car cuts for you. Whether the gearbox needs a downshift blip is not established, so blip to be safe; downshift clutch use is not established.
